extracted.intended_audience: pun competitors, performers, and judges (O. Henry Pun-Off and similar pun contests)
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric and procedural criteria for performing in and judging pun competitions (especially the O. Henry Pun-Off), covering prepared and head-to-head formats, timing, wordplay quality, audience reaction, and originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the pun relate to the assigned topic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For head-to-head Punslingers and any topic-based rounds, puns should clearly connect to the announced topic; topicality is explicitly judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordplay precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean homophone/homograph or other precise wordplay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for clean, precise instances of wordplay (e.g., homophones/homographs) where the dual reading is defensible rather than sloppy or ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Not a hoary old chestnut; not heard a million times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer fresh or unexpected twists rather than recycled, overused puns; originality is explicitly listed as a judging criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the audience react (groan or laugh)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience response (groans and laughs) is a visible scoring signal — groans count. Judging often uses audience reaction as a primary metric of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed of delivery / time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Performances and responses must meet time constraints (e.g., 90-second prepared piece; 5-second response in Punslingers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punniest of Show: 90-second prepared performance. Punslingers: 5 seconds to respond in head-to-head rounds. Being within time limits is a judged requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleverness versus strain (earned not forced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Puns should feel earned and clever, not forced or strained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges assess whether the substitution/wordplay is justified by sense as well as sound; forced or contrived puns score poorly even if technically correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pun density (prepared category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Density of puns within a prepared 90-second set matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Punniest of Show (prepared), competitors are evaluated on how many effective puns they pack into their allotted time — balancing density with clarity and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both meanings active (double reading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are both meanings active in context (two valid readings simultaneously)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong puns activate two legitimate readings at once; this criterion appears in the explicit rubric and the Pun Quality Heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution earned (sound + sense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the substitution earned — does it work for both sound and sense?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond phonetic similarity, the substituted word/phrase should make sense in context; 'sound-only' matches are weaker than sound+sense substitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illuminates something true
rubrics_metrics.description: The best puns illuminate something true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-tier puns do more than a clever twist; they reveal or highlight an insight, observation, or truth about the subject, which strengthens audience appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requiring explanation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a pun must be explained to be understood, it fails; effective puns are immediately apprehensible without post-hoc clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punslingers procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Head-to-head format rules: topic announced, two competitors trade puns, 5 seconds to respond, judge declares winner of each round, single-elimination tournament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are both procedural constraints and performance criteria—speed, topicality, and head-to-head competitiveness are enforced by format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging method: audience response as metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Judging often based on groans, laughs, and audience response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges and the contest use audience reaction (groans/laughter) as explicit scoring indicators; this emphasizes performative effect as well as technical merit.
